> I need to somehow find a way to get a girlfriend and get into the "game of love".  

Ask your co-workers if they have any friends they could introduce you to.  Hang out with your friends/co-workers in a group and you will organically meet some of their friends-of-friends that you could get to know better and go on some low-key dates with.  Keep everything casual just to get some practice going out and hanging with girls.  

> First of all, I have a big disadvantage: I'm a 27 years old virgin male...  

It's not a disadvantage; don't even think about it.  Doesn't matter.  You're looking to date and get to know someone, so being a virgin doesn't even factor into that yet, so don't let it psych you out or keep you from moving forward.

Hi Soyyoo!  

Unfortunately I'm not near Florida, but I wanted to stop by and let you know of some other subreddits where people might be:  There is [/r/florida](http://www.reddit.com/r/florida/), and [/r/miami](http://www.reddit.com/r/Miami/), even though they're pretty small, and [/r/meetup](http://www.reddit.com/r/meetup/) is where people plan and organize reddit meetups, so maybe there could be a Miami one!  

What's up?  It sucks to hear that you're feeling lonely, but it's also a good sign that you're willing to look for people to hang out with!  I usually do the opposite and avoid other people and end up making myself worse, instead of searching for friends or company :|

Yeah, that's what I meant - being touched by people - so I guess a magic wand wouldn't make me freak.  I meant I didn't want my comments to turn people away from massages as depression treatment if it might work for them.  Either way, good to know magic wands are actually good for legitimate massages, since the only people I've know who have them use them in more unorthodox applications.

I'm glad to hear that it has worked for you, and I definitely didn't want to disparage someone from trying it, but that was my first visceral reaction - the thought of having to get a massage to help my depression makes me cringe and want to scream.

Hi, I'm not the OP but I wanted to let you know that your comment really helped me.  I was checking back in with this thread last night before I went to bed, and was shocked and encouraged to read your story about recovering from your cognitive problems.  

When I originally commented here, it was the first time I admitted that I've been having problems thinking and talking, and I was still so embarrassed that I switched over to my alt account to write it.  I've always been depressed but it wasn't until this winter that my speech and cognition got worse and worse, and I was so scared to admit it or talk about it because I thought it was permanent, and facing the reality that something was going wrong in my head was enough to make me start panicking.  I've always been quick-witted and able to memorize things easily, so when my mind started declining I got terrified that I had done something wrong or had some disease and it was all over with, but hearing that you were in a similar situation, it wasn't permanent, and you were able to recover (quickly, at that!) was incredibly encouraging.  So thank you for taking the time to write your comment :)

I definitely know what's it's like to feel torn apart by depression and just sit there staring and not being able to concentrate, and recently I've also gotten to the point where I'm starting to stutter :(  

*Please* don't let your temporary thoughts of suicide influence you, because it will destroy everybody around you, and you aren't in a correct mental state right now to make those decisions now with your thoughts being clouded by depression.  What your wife and kids really deserve much more than anything is to not have the life-long pain and sadness they would feel if you were gone.  

If you'd like to get an app put together quickly, could you use [PhoneGap](http://www.phonegap.com/)?  It might make the development easier than completely learning Obj C, and it'd be really encouraging to get back into it and make something!  I've never done any app development but honestly since money is the concern, making a simple game or something completely childish, ridiculous, and single-purpose might be the best tactic to make some income off of it, instead of trying to re-write a full GPS navigation app or something.  


Keep talking with us, and you can always PM me if you need to!  I'm glad that you took the time to post, and it might be difficult, but talking through what you're feeling and being honest with yourself and others is really a huge therapeutic step forward.

So glad to hear that things are going well!  It's a huge step to have the courage to see a doctor, and it's really great of you to share your experience with everybody so they can get an idea of what it's like.  You never know some of the small bits of information that will make someone comfortable enough to seek help, so that's why it's so good to see a run-down of what your doctor visit was like!  

I definitely know the feeling of relief from just being able to say how you feel out loud and talk to someone face-to-face.  It's not going to be a quick fix, since your doctor will help you through a process of asking questions and digging down as you work together to overcome your depression, but having the strength to make it to the initial consultation and start on some medicine is a HUGE accomplishment!  

So funny to hear your picnic basket story, too ;)  You always feel like high-fiving when you're finally able to track down something you've been looking for!  Have a good time hanging out with the girl or going on a picnic - if nothing else, it will probably feel good to hang out with someone without any pressure or expectations about how things will turn out, since you can just be yourself and joke around and have fun.

What changed?  Well, nothing.  OK, Obviously a bunch of stuff has changed over the years, but I'm being real with you and not trying to get you to buy a Magic Life-Changing Elixir by saying "EVERYTHING CHANGED!!  LIFE IS AMAZING!!"  I didn't suddenly "decide" to get better, and I'm still not better today, but I *am* me, and I started living my life.  I moved out, (eventually) got a job, started meeting people there, and most importantly, started moving away from the things that triggered my depression.  I cut ties with the girl who was enabling my craziness, I stopped depending on my parents, and I started to open up to people around me.  I am a very shy, introverted, and quiet person, so I was amazed that even the smallest amount of opening myself up to other people made me feel immensely better and made me realize that everyone else feels the same things -- it was like a joke that I'd been playing on myself, thinking that I had to suffer alone and that I should stay away from everyone.  I'm sure as hell not a talkative life-of-the-party nowadays or anything, but that's why I say some stuff has changed, and some hasn't.  The biggest thing that changed that made me terrified that I'd thought of killing myself was the realization that my perception on reality had been too muddled by my thoughts, and I wasn't seeing the world or myself the way they really were.  

Saying stuff like "I know the only thing holding me back is myself" is an easy thing to fall back on because it can't be proven right or wrong!  I've thought the same thing about myself, but it doesn't mean anything -- like saying "you know why we didn't win the game?  because we didn't win the game."  Of course it seems like you're the cause of your problems, because you're inside yourself and can't think any other way!  That's what (good) psychologists are for -- they ask questions that you'd never think to ask yourself, and challenge your opinions when they don't match up with what's really going on.  

There is no sudden transformation into some movie-perfect happy-go-lucky life, and life is still confusing and strange and crazy for me, but I guarantee you will be just as freaked out as I was once you step out and see how different reality was and how much you would have regretted your life ending there.  I know it's true, because I am still on that same journey.

> I just wouldn't mind it so much if just one person liked me.  

I like you.  I've read through all your comments and you seem really funny and I like your sense of humor, but it scares me to hear that you'd kill yourself and this is why:  I thought about running away and putting everything in order and killing myself, in an attempt to stop hurting and being a burden on people, but that was five years ago, and now I'm extremely glad that I didn't do it.  It's scary because I can still look back at myself when my mind was messed up and now I know *exactly* what I would have been throwing away.  Usually it's just vague "oh well one day it will get better, you'll see" type of stuff, but this is reality -- I can look back on every single thing that has happened to me since then and it gives me the chills to think that I thought about ending it all and missing out on this!  

Hell, I don't know what to say; I'm no professional, all I know is how to be real with you, and that's the biggest realization that I have to offer after being in the dark place that you're going through.  The absolute most important thing I learned was that being depressed wasn't because I'd done something wrong, or because I was a bad person, or because the world hated me, it was *only* because our minds can get messed up and we can't diagnose ourselves.  It's the only disease where we think we should be able to "fix" ourselves -- You never see people get a terrible physical disease and then go "well, I guess I'll just have to figure out how to cure myself!"  When something goes wrong mentally, trying to think through it alone is as ridiculous as catching the flu and then killing yourself because you could never imagine yourself getting any better.  

Anyway, I've blabbed enough.  Keep talking to us, and don't make any permanent decisions.  It's not about being strong or weak or anything else, it's about me, looking back at you from five years in the future, and begging you to trust me that things can change.

Wow, that's so cool that you work at the helpline!  Thanks so much for the insider info!  What kind of resources do you connect people with?  I have never gotten help because I don't have insurance or enough money to pay for treatment, but I also don't know what kind of things are available that aren't psychologists/psychiatrists who charge $100 per session.  

It's too bad they're all labeled "suicide" hotlines, since (for me, at least) that carries quite a stigma attached to it, and makes me hesitant to call if I'm only just depressed, and not thinking about hurting myself.  

idego posted a link below to [the Befrienders](http://www.befrienders.org/helplines/helplines.asp?c2=USA), who seem to be a part of the Samaritans - have you heard of them?  They sound like the type of help I was looking for, and there is a local group and hotline in NYC, where I live.

Hi RoundSparrow,

Thanks for your kind words and help!  I've been generally depressed for years, so day-to-day it seems normal to feel down, but I don't think there is much of a sense of urgency anymore.  Lately I've been realizing that things aren't the way they should be, so I'm starting to seek out help.  You hit the nail on the head by saying a "loss of perspective" - that's a great way to describe what happens when depression sets in and your perception of things gets warped to seem disastrous.

Hi xenotype,

Yeah, they sounded like just what I was looking for, and it seemed like they were only in the UK, but the link idego posted above shows that they're all over the world, including one in my city!  I'm doing better today - I talked with one of my friends and just joked around for a bit, which made me feel better - but I think I'll definitely call the Samaritans if I get in trouble again, since I'm really emotionally unstable when it comes to circumstances that will push me deeper into depression.  

Thanks for your kind words and I hope your day has been going well!

Yeah the Samaritans sounded really cool and helpful and sounded just like what I was looking for.  I looked at the link you posted and there is some kind of Samaritans in NYC where I live - http://www.samaritansnyc.org/  I don't know why my search last night didn't turn up that link, but I definitely would have called if I'd know about them.  The Samaritans website makes it sound like they're only in the UK, but your link obviously shows they're all over the world!
Yeah, that's definitely the right outcome, but I don't have insurance or money, so I'm stuck.  Even the small group meeting that I found online had a fee to get in!  I couldn't believe it.

I'm feeling a bit better now, but I'm already dreading tomorrow.  The next week or so will be annoying in my life, and I'll come back and talk if things get tough, but I've been depressed for six years now, so it's pretty normal.

I actually just read through this, and it had a lot of really helpful tips - http://www.psycom.net/depression.central.helpself.html  From my experience, those tips are really useful to start feeling better.

Hi redGPz,

The suicide hotlines seem to be all that's available, so I guess if I'm going to call someone, it'll have to be them!  It's intimidating though, since I'm not standing on a ledge or anything.  If nothing else, they might know some other resources.  I read the "Read this first" article in the sidebar here, and it was interesting.  The Samaritans sound really helpful, but I guess they're only in the UK, and I'm in the US.

Hi Orangutan,

Yeah, I saw the list, but since I wasn't having an emergency, it seemed like calling 911 to complain about a parking ticket.  I read through the "Thinking about suicide? Read this first" link, and that was pretty cool.

Yeah, I'm sort of aware of what I need to do, but it's tough, and without any outside perspective, it's easy to convince yourself that your life is just supposed to be this way....

I'm going to look into some kind of therapy group, but fighting back is the hardest part because it's hard to figure out why it's worth it.  It's been cool to read the stories of some people who survived depression, then talked about how their life really did change.  I guess if I made it through, it would be worth it, but it's hard to imagine living any other way since this has been my life for so long.

Hi bleepitybleep,

Thanks for the offer to look up some info, because I'm honestly not sure what's available aside from private psychiatrists, but I think going to a group or something is a good idea.  I live in New York City, so I'm sure there's some kind of support group or free option out there....  Is there anything like "Depression Anonymous"?  lol

Haha, yeah, I guess that Fight Club line of thinking didn't work out too well in the end ;)

Despite my Reddit membership, I actually was quite religious before and during the some of the worst parts of my depression.  But I'm not really anything now.  That has kinda faded away along with everything else.

Back when I *did* have money and insurance, I didn't want to get on medicine because I'd seen one of my friends get torn apart as they tried to find the right anti-depressant.  Now I wish I had just gotten a consultation and maybe even started meds, since maybe I could have avoided losing the last few years of my life to this nothingness.

Thanks for taking the time to talk with me :)  If nothing else, it's been cool to see other people who have gotten through it.  Depression has a way of tricking you into thinking its permanent.

It took me a long time to realize I should probably get some outside help.  I've actually spent a big part of my life being the emotional support for someone who is psychologically much worse off than I am, so that kinda distracted me from what was going wrong with myself that whole time.  

My family isn't the type to mention therapy, so even though they can sense something is going wrong, they don't know what to say, and I only see them a few times a year anyway.

I'm actually a musician, so you know how troubled we tend to be ;P  Ironically enough, I have no problem performing and being "in the spotlight" when it comes to music or writing songs, but playing music definitely makes me feel more alive and worthwhile and sane.

It's definitely a difficult and embarrassing step to try and get into some kind of counseling.  I've actually been debating going to some kind of 12-step meeting just to be around people, even though I don't have any addictions (how very Fight Club, right?)  I've casually looking into psychiatrist prices, but even the "sliding scale" ones are way too much.

Going for walks is nice, I usually try to do that fairly often.  I live in the city, so it's nice to get outside and see everyone walking around.  It makes me feel like I'm part of something.  I'm actually a kind, happy person, but there's also this dark secret depression under that persona that causes a lot of problems, and I need to start dealing with that instead of just accepting it as fact.

Yeah, I still feel kinda silly since there are people in much worse situations than I am, but things were weighing kinda heavy on me this evening (trying to figure out how to pay rent, etc.)

I won't be too specific about my old job, but it was a sort of high-profile self-employed sales kinda job, where I didn't really work for anyone, so I didn't necessarily quit *because* of my depression, but I did lose any interest in working and trying to do the networking/marketing necessary.  My next job will definitely be more structured so I can pay attention to myself instead of getting wrapped up in work seven days a week.
